speaker: Doctor
text: Those initial screening tests came back normal, which is helpful, but your symptoms of night sweats, weight loss, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are concerning for malignancy or a specific chronic infection. Have you noticed any skin changes, such as itching or a rash, or any changes in your stool consistency? REQUEST IMAGES: Lymph_Node_Ultrasound, PET_C.Scan

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Adult T-cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL) associated with HTLV-1 infection. The combination of supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, drenching night sweats, rapid weight loss, abdominal pain, and normal initial screening tests (ruling out common bacterial infections and HIV) strongly suggests this malignancy, which is endemic in certain regions and often presents with lytic bone lesions or hypercalcemia not yet captured by our limited panel. I recommend immediate testing for HTLV-1 and a Calcium level to confirm this suspicion.
